metadata.case_name: CHEUNG YUK LIN v. SUN TAK MING AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_before: dance hostess at the Oriental Ballroom

injuries.description:
Facial scars and deformities as described by Dr. Leung Kwok-on: 1. Trap-door deformity at forehead due to one 2.5 cm long curve scar.
2. Uneven 3 cm long scar extending from the right upper eyelid to root of nose.
3. Uneven 2 cm long scar extending from the left upper eyelid to root of nose.
4. 1.5 cm long scar on the left side of bridge of nose.
5. 4 cm long curve scar with contracture at left maxillary region resulting in ectropion of the left lower eyelid and inability of left eye to close completely.
6. 1.5 cm long uneven scar on lateral aspect of the left upper eyelid.
7. Numerous small scars scattered around forehead.
8. Small scar on the left cheek area.
source: On admission to hospital immediately after the accident the plaintiff was found to have sustained 9 lacerations to her face. These were cleansed and sutured and after six days of hospitalisation she was released and thereafter attended an outpatient clinic.

Dr. Leung Kwok-on gave evidence of the nature of the plaintiff's injuries. He said her facial scars are as follows:

1. Trap-door deformity at forehead due to one 2.5 cm long curve scar.  
2. Uneven 3 cm long scar extending from the right upper eyelid to root of nose.  
3. Uneven 2 cm long scar extending from the left upper eyelid to root of nose.  
4. 1.5 cm long scar on the left side of bridge of nose.  
5. 4 cm long curve scar with contracture at left maxillary region resulting in ectropion of the left lower eyelid and inability of left eye to close completely.  
6. 1.5 cm long uneven scar on lateral aspect of the left upper eyelid.  
7. Numerous small scars scattered around forehead.  
8. Small scar on the left cheek area.  

He said the above scars were disfiguring and involved a significant portion of the face. He was of the opinion that they could all be improved by plastic surgery, but that several sessions would be required. He said that these included multiple Z-plasties, blepharoplasties, revisions and two dermabrasions. Furthermore she would need repeated hospitalisation and anaesthetics at intervals of approximately four months. Dr. Leung said that his present quote for carrying out the necessary cosmetic surgery, including hospitalisation and anaesthetics, would be about $32,000 on a 3rd class patient basis. He said that treatment on a 1st class patient basis would cost double that amount and that treatment on a 2nd class patient basis would cost about 50% more than that on a 3rd class patient basis. 1st class patient treatment involves a single room, 2nd class treatment a 2 to 3 patient room with better treatment than that given in 3rd class. 3rd class treatment is given in an open ward involving a higher chance of infection post surgery. He said that the risk of infection was not high but most patients have second class treatment.

manifestations.description: Facial scarring and disfigurement (disfiguring and involved a significant portion of the face)
Ectropion of the left lower eyelid and inability of left eye to close completely
Persistent headaches and dizziness, insomnia, phobia and frequent lapses of memory
Anxiety - depression as a result of psychological and physical trauma sustained in the accident

treatments_received: sutures/cleansing of 9 facial lacerations (operation lasted about 1½ hours) performed under local anaesthesia
consultations with Dr. Peter Wu and others
treatments_future: cosmetic/plastic surgery consisting of multiple Z-plasties, blepharoplasties, revisions and two dermabrasions (a course of about five operations)
repeated hospitalisation and anaesthetics at intervals of approximately four months

losses.description: I have no doubt that the plaintiff in the present case has suffered a great deal of anxiety over her appearance. Although this is a subjective matter it is one which is readily understandable. Facial disfigurement is most distressing for a young woman particularly if, as in this case, she is unmarried.

Assessment of loss of future earnings on the basis of a multiplicand of $2,500 and a multiplier of two (reflecting loss in employment/earnings capacity resulting from her facial disfigurement and treatment period).

comparable_cases.injury_description: Facial injuries more serious than present case; plaintiff attempted suicide twice; awarded $50,000 under this head
Facial injuries comparable to present case; award of $15,000 under this head to young married woman aged 18
